evidence.description: Initialization launches credential restoration without retaining or awaiting the task.
Credential retrieval updates tokens and login status after an asynchronous provider call.
Logout clears local tokens and the profile independently of pending authentication requests.
The user-info request assigns the profile after suspension without verifying that its session is still current.

candidates.explanation: Authentication operations can finish after a later logout and overwrite its state. Initialization starts credential retrieval in an untracked task, and retrieval applies credentials after awaiting the provider without checking whether logout occurred meanwhile. Similarly, an in-flight user-info request can repopulate userProfile after logout clears it. There is no visible cancellation or operation-validity check protecting these updates.
candidates.title: Pending authentication work can undo logout

evidence.description: SSO credentials are retained as service state.
Successful login updates primary credentials but does not update or invalidate SSO credentials.
Logout invokes a helper that clears primary tokens and login status but does not clear ssoCredentials.
The token-update helper does not modify SSO credentials.
Cookie generation only checks login status before using the retained SSO credentials.

candidates.explanation: Logout clears the primary tokens but leaves ssoCredentials intact. A subsequent login sets isLoggedIn back to true without replacing those SSO credentials, so getSessionTokenCookie can create a cookie using the previous session's transfer token. This retains authentication material across session boundaries and can mix credentials from different users.
candidates.title: SSO credentials survive logout

evidence.description: Local token clearing occurs only when clearCredentials returns true.
The failure branch neither throws nor clears local state when there is no session error and credentials cannot be renewed.

candidates.explanation: When clearCredentials returns false, no web-session error exists, and canRenewCredentials returns false, logout returns normally without clearing any in-memory authentication state. The ability to renew credentials does not establish whether the service still holds an access token or reports isLoggedIn as true. This branch can therefore report successful completion while leaving the local session active.
candidates.title: Logout can silently leave local authentication active

evidence.description: The profile setter posts the profile-update notification.
A throwing cache operation occurs between token clearing and profile clearing.

candidates.explanation: Image-cache cleanup is awaited with try before userProfile is cleared. If cache cleanup throws, logout exits after clearing credentials and login status but retains the previous user's profile and never posts the profile-cleared notification triggered by its setter. An ancillary cache failure thus leaves partially cleared authentication state.
candidates.title: Cache cleanup failure prevents profile clearing

evidence.description: A false storage result throws credentialsStorageFailed, which the enclosing catch immediately wraps as credentialsStorageError.

candidates.explanation: The credentialsStorageFailed error thrown when storage returns false is inside the same do block whose catch wraps every error as credentialsStorageError. Consequently, callers never receive credentialsStorageFailed directly from this path, losing the distinction between a false storage result and a thrown storage error.
candidates.title: Storage failure error is immediately rewrapped
